[element-std-id-group]
=== `<std-id-group>` Standard ID Group

A container element that holds one or more standard identifiers (<<element-std-id,`<std-id>`>>s) to indicate that they are alternative identifiers for the same standard, for example, one <<element-std-id,`<std-id>`>> for a DOI and one <<element-std-id,`<std-id>`>> for a URN.

#### Usage/Remarks
The <<attribute-std-relationship-type,`@std-relationship-type`>> attribute can be used to define how a specific identifier or group of identifiers is related to the current standard, for example, whether the identifiers are part of a standard set or are adoptions of the standard.

#### Attributes

* <<attribute-originator,`@originator`>>
* <<attribute-specific-use,`@specific-use`>>
* <<attribute-std-relationship-type,`@std-relationship-type`>>

<std-id-group 
  std-relationship-type="std-as-published">

   std-id-type="dated">ASME A17.1-2013/CSA B44-13</std-id>
 <std-id 
   std-id-type="dated" 
   std-id-link-type="doi">10.1115/ASME A17.1-2013/CSA B44-13</std-id>
</std-id-group>

<std-id-group 
  std-relationship-type="std-as-published">
 <std-id

   std-id-link-type="doi">10.1115/ASME A17.1/CSA B44</std-id>
</std-id-group>

<std-id-group 
  std-relationship-type="std-as-published">
 <std-id 
   std-id-type="short" 
   std-relationship-type="std-family">A17</std-id>
 <std-id 
   std-id-type="short" 
   std-id-link-type="doi">10.1115/ASME.A17</std-id>
</std-id-group>

<std-id-group 
  originator="CSA" 
  std-relationship-type="std-alt-as-published">
 <std-id 
   std-id-type="dated">CSA B44-13</std-id>
 <std-id 
   std-id-type="dated" 
   std-id-link-type="doi">10.XYZ/CSA.B44-13</std-id>
</std-id-group>
...
....
